question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)={7}^{x-2}+4.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={7}^{x-2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={7}^{y-2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={7}^{y-2}+4 \\ x-4 & ={7}^{y-2} \\ {log}_{7}⁡(x-4) & ={log}_{7}⁡({7}^{y-2}) \\ {log}_{7}⁡(x-4) & =y-2 \\ y & ={log}_{7}⁡(x-4)+2\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)={log}_{7}⁡(x-4)+2.$
